content: Laurel water is a liquid distilled from the fresh leaves of the cherry laurel plant. It contains prussic acid, also known as hydrocyanic acid, which is a highly toxic compound. During the distillation process, other substances are also carried over into the final product. In terms of pharmacological applications, laurel water (referred to in Latin as aqua laurocerasi) has historically been used to treat conditions such as asthma, cough, indigestion, and dyspepsia. It has also been employed as a sedative narcotic. However, because laurel water is essentially a solution of hydrogen cyanide with an unpredictable concentration, its use as a medication is extremely hazardous and poses significant risks to health. Historically, it is documented that the Roman emperor Nero utilized cherry laurel water as a means to poison the water supplies of his adversaries.
